### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS (symbol, a top-level const object), PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8cc0b2b9f735db8438f20c3467dd6d4a9c695a65` — the merge of head `36864c49d17a7b6ef8321ce2d90a6f3d6183f24e` into base `09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8cc0b2b9f735db8438f20c3467dd6d4a9c695a65 && git checkout 8cc0b2b9f735db8438f20c3467dd6d4a9c695a65
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a 36864c49d17a7b6ef8321ce2d90a6f3d6183f24e && git checkout -B drift-repro 09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a && git merge --no-ff 36864c49d17a7b6ef8321ce2d90a6f3d6183f24e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 09bf7de71f3a490eae3abe7a03559cb914e2af7a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `36864c49d17a7b6ef8321ce2d90a6f3d6183f24e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts + none

Read: card #32011 (body and all 4 comments: triage 6755180754, claim 6755947891, amendment 6755995440, dev report 6756948687), PR #32039 (body, the 4-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge-base `60f8149e`), and the check-runs on this head. No file in the diff implements or enforces the `hits` file apart from itself: the other three paths are two test files and one changeset, which are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Code read to judge, not reviewed: `classifyRequiredCapability` (same file, unchanged), `validateKnownCapabilities` in `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`, the `requires` resolver in `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/capability-preflight.ts`, `packages/core/src/capability-providers.ts`, `packages/verify/src/required-providers.ts`, `packages/cli/test/serve-capability-vocabulary.test.ts`.

Check-runs on the head, all concluded: 0 failure, 0 cancelled, 0 pending. Success on every family that ran, among them `Test Core` (8/8 shards), `TypeScript Type Check` (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), `Lint & Repo Gates` (all scoped legs), `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Test UI` (16/16), `Live E2E UI`. Skipped by their own path filters or opt-in: `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`, `UI Published Artifacts`, `Lint UI`, the two queue verdicts, the two opt-in harnesses.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of `requires` (`defineStack`, through `validateKnownCapabilities`, which reads `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS.includes`): widens by exactly two values, `audit-compliance` and `access-policy-console`. Right, and it is what the card asks. Nothing that parsed before parses differently; no value is removed or respelled. The match is verbatim, so `audit_compliance`, `auditCompliance`, `access-policy` and `access_policy_console` stay `STACK_CAPABILITY_UNKNOWN`. Right.
- Public surface: no export added, removed or retyped. `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS` and `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` keep their types and each gains two members; the api-surface and export-origins ledgers list names only and correctly do not move. Right.
- `os build` / `os validate` preflight: both tokens classify `unavailable` for every `isInstalled`, because `package` is `null` (the first branch of `classifyRequiredCapability` is skipped) and `edition` is `cloud`. That is a fatal preflight error reading "provided only by a cloud runtime and has no open-edition provider (cloud audit-compliance tier)". Same as `governance`. Right for the open edition.
- `objectstack serve`: neither token keys a `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` row in `@objectstack/core`, both are in the vocabulary, so the resolver skips them without a word. Same as `ai-seat` / `governance`; inherited behaviour, not introduced here. Right as a derivation; see ④ finding 2 for what it means while no runtime provides them.
- Drift test (`serve-capability-vocabulary.test.ts`): the 1:1 pin between vocabulary and provider map holds (two tokens, two rows); the open-edition and enterprise pins do not see `cloud` rows; `PLATFORM_ALWAYS_ON_CAPABILITIES` is untouched. No edit was needed there. Right. `Test Core` is green on the merged tree.
- `packages/verify` boot: a token with no `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` row mounts nothing, as in `serve`. Unchanged. Right.
- Generated output: none owed. The vocabulary is a frozen constant, not a Zod schema, and no reference page enumerates it. Right; the generated-artefact legs are green.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor` is right. A new accepted `requires` value is `Metadata-protocol: added`, and AGENTS.md has that kind take at least `minor` on the package the diff moves. No other released package is moved by the diff, so no second entry is owed. `skip-changeset` does not apply.

Clause-②: yes (widening: two new accepted `requires` tokens). The line is present and identical in the PR body and the changeset body, with `Metadata-protocol: added` beside it; `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head. No `(narrowing)` arm applies: no value is refused that was accepted on `main`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: empty. One question should have been there and is escalated by this record: the card's Ask 2 says "Use the provider package names that cloud's loader resolves, and ask the cloud lane if they are not readable here." Cloud code is not readable in this repo, the question was not asked, and the rows ship `package: null`. Escalated to the cloud lane as ④ finding 1. It is not listed among the dev's deviations either.
- Deviation "origin/main moved 8 commits, branch not re-merged": answered. None of the 8 commits touches the three source paths of this diff (measured: empty diff of those paths between `60f8149e` and `09bf7de7`), and CI ran the merged tree green.
- Deviation "test:repo not run locally": answered by `Test Core` and `Lint & Repo Gates` on the head.
- Deviations on PR-body line order and on assignee/reviewer: process shape, no contract effect; `PR-body guards` concluded success. Accepted.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` for `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` L318-320: the sentence there ("`ai-seat` and `governance` are resolved only by cloud's objectos-runtime") stays true and does not claim to be the whole set, and the same section names `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS` as the authoritative list. Accepted as a follow-up; it names no card yet, so the seat owes it a carrier.
- Out-of-scope notes (`serve.ts:5370` comment, `stack.zod.ts:6227` docblock): both name the older tokens as examples and neither is falsified. Accepted as noted. The `stack.zod.ts` docblock calls `ai-seat` / `governance` "enterprise plugin-provided", which was already loose on `main`; outside this diff.
- File surface: the diff stays inside the claimed surface (the `hits` file, its two test files, one changeset). No cloud code, no CLI provider, no `ui/**`. Held.
- Security: none found. The change grants nothing; a token in `requires` is a declaration of need, not an authorization.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts`, judged against card #32011 (the ask and triage 6755180754), the file's own contract prose, and its first consumers in this repo (`defineStack`, the preflight, `serve`).

The token hunk and the two provider rows do what the card asks and agree with every sentence of the contract that can be checked here: the 1:1 map invariant, the kebab-case spelling rule, the `CapabilityEdition` definition of `cloud` ("no installable version in the open edition"), and the `unavailable` branch of the classifier. The group placement after `governance` and the notes follow the existing rows. Attempts to break it: a near-miss spelling (refused, verbatim match); confusion with the existing open-edition `audit` token (distinct string, distinct row, no prefix matching anywhere in the read paths); a silent `installable` hint pointing at a package no registry has (not reachable, `package` is `null`); an always-on or tier interaction (none, neither token is on the slate or in `CAPABILITY_TO_TIER`). None broke.

1. should-fix — `package: null` on both rows was decided without the answer the card told the dev to get. The card's Ask 2 asks for the package names cloud's loader resolves and says to ask the cloud lane if they are not readable; they are not readable here, nobody asked, and the diff instead asserts in the `PlatformCapabilityProvider.package` docblock that both are "a cloud-runtime tier with no standalone package to install". That sentence is a published statement of fact about cloud that this repo cannot verify, and the test `are exactly the package-less rows` pins it. In the open edition the choice changes nothing (both spellings classify `unavailable`). It matters where the provider is installed: the file's header says cloud's runtime and the CLI "classify a `requires` token identically", and a `null` row classifies `unavailable` even with the provider present, where a named `cloud` row (the `ai` / `ai-studio` shape) classifies `ok`. Fix: put the question to the cloud lane on card #32011 and record the answer there. If the answer is "no standalone package, same as `governance`", nothing in the tree moves and this record still covers the head. If cloud names packages, the two rows, the docblock and the pin test follow, which moves the head and owes a delta review.

2. should-fix — the tokens are published before any runtime provides them, and the consumer has no carrier. By the card's own account cloud's loader does not resolve either token today: it "adds the two `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` entries" only after a pin that contains this change, in a cloud card that is to be filed "when this lands". Until then `defineStack` accepts two values no runtime delivers, while this file's header still says the vocabulary is "the union of every token the framework CLI and cloud's objectos-runtime resolve", the new group comment says both "are resolved by cloud's objectos-runtime loader only" in the present tense, and `serve` stays quiet on them. The open edition is not misled, because the preflight fails the build; the gap is the unbounded window on the cloud side (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 10, declared is not enforced). Spec-first is the only order the drift pins allow, so the order itself is accepted. Fix, on the prose faces only: file or name the cloud consumer card now and cite its number on #32011 and in the PR body's `Carried:` line, so the window has an owner and an end. No tree change is asked.

3. nit — the group comment now carries two different claims in one parenthesis ("no open-edition provider" for the group, then "this repository installs nothing for them" for the four cloud tokens). Both are true. The second is redundant with the provider rows; leave it.

4. nit — `note: 'cloud access-policy console'` breaks the "cloud X tier" pattern of its three siblings, and the preflight renders it inside a sentence that ends "run under a cloud runtime that provides the "access-policy-console" tier". Readable either way; an accepted deviation.

No must-fix. Findings 1 and 2 each earn a delta review of their fix; both can close on the prose faces without moving this head, unless the cloud lane's answer to 1 names packages.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`requires` 新接受两个能力 token：`audit-compliance` 和 `access-policy-console`，与 `governance` 同组（只由云端 objectos-runtime 加载器提供）；provider 表各加一行，`package: null`、`edition: 'cloud'`，与 `governance` 同形。
- 为什么改：云端有这两项按环境开通的能力，没有 token 就无法在 stack 里声明，云端只能把它们标成不可用。
- 风险与回滚：只放宽；原来能过的照旧能过，近似拼写（`audit_compliance`、`access-policy`）照旧拒收。本仓不装任何包，开源版 `os build` 对这两个 token 的处理与 `governance` 完全一致（判为仅云端可用并失败）。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts`（token 组与两行 provider）；`packages/spec/src/stack-requires.test.ts` 新增的 describe。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/stack-requires.test.ts src/kernel/platform-capabilities.test.ts`，预期 2 个文件全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。


席位意见：fable 契约复审一轮 PASS（6757357654），无必改，两条建议改都不需要动代码。建议改 2（消费方载体）已把 cloud#4218 写进 PR 正文的 `Carried:` 行。建议改 1（两个令牌在云端是否有安装包）已在 #32011 上问 cloud 车道（02:36Z），至今未答；本 PR 按 `governance` 先例写 `package: null`，这是接受的偏差。若云端日后给出包名，只需改 provider 行这一处数据，另开卡处理，不阻塞本卡。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:spec#3 · head `36864c49d17a7b6ef8321ce2d90a6f3d6183f24e`

- **Shape:** 4 files (+100 −3) on merge-base `60f8149e`: two tokens in the cloud-loader group of `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS` with the group comment naming all four; two `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` rows `{ package: null, edition: 'cloud', note }`; pins in `platform-capabilities.test.ts` and `stack-requires.test.ts`; `@objectstack/spec` minor changeset.
- **Premise measured:** at `60f8149e` the cloud-loader group ended `hierarchy-security`, `ai-seat`, `governance`, and neither new token appeared anywhere in the repo (claim 6755947891).
- **Gates:** check-runs on this head: 60 success, 15 skipped, 0 red, `mergeable_state` clean. Dev report 6756948687: spec 26276 pass, typecheck 0, `check:generated` 0, CLI drift + preflight 38/38, ablation 4 red / 75 green, 85/85 derived gates exit 0 with `--ran` 0 NOT-MEASURED, `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0 with the body (control 1).
- **Contract review:** 6757357654 on this head, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, schema face: PASS, no must-fix; should-fix 1 and 2 answered above, both on prose faces or the card, so the head did not move.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes (widening: two new accepted `requires` tokens)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, `@objectstack/spec` minor; `Skills-docs: follow-up #32041` (filed by the seat; the dev's `owed` rewritten in body r1). Changeset sentences checked against the diff: both tokens, `package: null`, `edition: 'cloud'`, and the near-miss refusals each match a pinned case.
- **Accepted deviations:** `package: null` for both rows without the cloud lane's answer (above); `note: 'cloud access-policy console'` breaks the "cloud X tier" pattern of its siblings (nit); the group comment's "this repository installs nothing for them" repeats the rows (nit); branch not re-merged with `main` (13 first-parent commits, no overlap; CI ran the merged tree green).
- **Carried:** objectstack-ai/cloud#4218: cloud's loader adds the two providers after a pin carries this (PR body `Carried:` line).
- **Landing:** not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 32039`: 103 lines, 0 governed paths), Tier S. The relay landing stroke is refused in this session by the auto-mode classifier ("Merge Without Review", first met on PR #32034 at 02:16Z); the seat has asked the maintainer to ready it or allow the stroke, and does not re-spell it. The PR stays draft, ACCEPTed and green.
